[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations] In 2025 and 2026, Iran and the United States began a series of negotiations aimed at reaching a nuclear peace agreement, following a letter from US president Donald Trump to Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei, setting a 60-day deadline for Iran to reach an agreement. After the deadline passed without an agreement in June 2025, Israel launched airstrikes against Iran, starting the Twelve-Day War. As of June 28, 2026, there were three rounds of talks before the Islamabad talks that led to the Islamabad Memorandum, and two rounds of technical talks. The first round was held in Oman on April 12, 2025, led by US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi. A second round of Omani-mediated talks took place in Rome on April 19, 2025, again between Witkoff and Araghchi. This was followed by a third round in Muscat around a week later; an expert-level meeting to develop a framework for a possible nuclear agreement was led by Michael Anton for the US and by Majid Takht-Ravanchi for Iran. The US military had been building up its presence in the Middle East as the threat of war escalated. US bases throughout the region accommodate approximately 50,000 American troops. As part of the peace proposals, Iran proposed building at least 19 additional reactors, suggesting that American involvement in these projects could help revitalize the US nuclear industry. A planned address by Araghchi to formally announce this proposal was ultimately cancelled. On May 27, Trump said both sides were close to finalizing an agreement involving strong inspections. Araghchi stated he was unsure whether a deal was imminent, while Khamenei's advisor, Ali Shamkhani, dismissed Trump's desired control over the Iranian nuclear program as a "fantasy". [Iran–United States relations during the second Trump administration] Relations between Iran and the United States during Donald Trump's second term as the president of the United States (2025–present) were shaped by diplomatic pressure and military conflict. In February 2026, he launched a major attack on Iran with Israel with the stated goal of regime change, during which Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, was killed. In February 2025, Trump reinstated the "maximum pressure" campaign against Iran, and in March he sent a letter to Khamenei proposing new nuclear negotiations, and warning of possible military action if talks failed. As indirect contact failed to reach an agreement, Israel launched a surprise attack on Iran on June 13, striking nuclear and military targets, and beginning the 12-day war. The US joined Israel with direct strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities, including Fordow on June 22. A ceasefire took place on June 24. Diplomatic contact resumed intermittently over the following months. Beginning in late 2025, Iran experienced widespread anti-government protests that were met with a violent crackdown. In January 2026, Trump warned of possible military action if Iranian authorities crossed an unspecified "red line", encouraging the protestors to escalate demonstrations, and building up US forces in the region. Indirect negotiations resumed between Iranian and US officials in Oman in early February 2026. On February 28, the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran aimed at regime change. Among those killed was Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and several of his family members. Khamenei's death was confirmed by Iran on March 01. The strikes prompted celebrations among some Iranians and members of the Iranian diaspora, along with mourning and protest against the war, both within Iran and internationally. Opinion polls have indicated that most Americans do not approve of the war; however, Trump has dismissed polls, saying that he doesn't care.
